batch_strategy: Select matched condition segments and loading contrasts where new labels can distinguish response shapes, repair demonstrated endpoint failures, or constrain recurring Row inputs. Include one deliberate repeat to test a consequential loading-dependent trough; reduce follow-up on families whose latest interiors were accurately predicted.

choices.reason: m32 at pure EA, 50 uL tests whether the elevated 150-uL baseline in 70dd45e8e1ff8116c181 extends to lower loading. Its current completion prediction is 13.53 mL; measured 50-uL 1/1 and 2/1 completions are 7.88 and 8.24 in 9eec792e8b2ea194dd3c and d73810c9779aede1ff57. This locates the strong-side decrease without transferring the 150-uL curve wholesale.

Deliberately repeat m32 at 5/1, 150 uL. The existing completion is 10.98 in 6ece01a2e0fc9b1585df, versus 21.36 at 10/1 in 7c11aaa0d5d18caa8c92. The 100-uL repeat changed completion from 18.56 to 15.05, so checking this high-loading trough is more informative than assuming its magnitude is reproducible.

m155 at pure EA, 50 uL supplies the missing baseline before the newly measured 1/1 response of 7.65/11.77 in 73771d4752cdcd04a023. The current baseline prediction is 4.05/5.59, while pure EA at 100 uL measured 4.07/6.72 in b213664a8c509420288b. This tests whether the newly exposed failure is localized around 1/1.

m155 at 5/1, 100 uL tests the predicted return to approximately 5.55/8.20 after the measured 1/1 completion of 13.72 in 98923a8da3524ce0e392. The 50-uL 5/1 label c4c961533c50b899078c measured 6.08/8.10 accurately. This separates a ratio-local completion problem from a broader loading-dependent offset.

m82 at 1/1, 150 uL fills the missing strong-side loading contrast. The 100-uL counterpart finishes at 14.95 in 5f189f103424c7cfda69, and the 150-uL 2/1 anchor c5130d0b1bb6dba0fb85 finishes at 19.77. This asks whether the pronounced loading dependence newly seen at 5/1 begins this early in the curve.

m95 at 1/1, 50 uL extends the methyl acetoacetate comparison to m82. Its measured 100-uL 1/1 completion is 12.88 in 598ca66d9a8305ded243, and its 50-uL 5/1 completion is 23.20 in cd566862a517dd7cdc8d. The new label constrains where completion growth begins without assuming that m82's stronger low-loading response transfers to another ester.

m78 at pure EA, 100 uL starts a matched strong-side pair for a benzyl-substituted beta-ketoester. The predictor places completion at 9.53 mL and slightly lower at 1/1. Measuring the baseline and its counterpart tests this predicted decrease in a carbonyl environment distinct from m82 and m95; 6000105cb6734cff8146 provides a measured 150-uL 5/1 reference.

m78 at 1/1, 100 uL completes the pair, predicted at 5.38/9.31. The label distinguishes a genuine strong-side completion decrease from an interpolation artifact before its established later response, including 25.00-mL completion at 10/1, 50 uL in 9ccd4f4f61665ec641fe and 43.60 at 20/1, 100 uL in a44a22945d76c02aa6a7.

m104 at 5/1, 150 uL connects measured 1/1 completion 13.47 in 79515e25d0daceed2ce8 with 20/1 completion 9.45 in 6c4eacf7845534254af9. Comparison with the 100-uL 5/1 completion of 13.90 in 645cb06b9e2a33b6044b locates any high-loading turnover while avoiding a universal correction from the unusual new 100-uL 1/1 onset.

m12 at pure EA, 100 uL establishes the baseline before measured completion growth through 1/1, 2/1 and 5/1 in afbb3431f3c1f6b3fc84, 35e055b13ba20e843f0d and dbe79bb4ca4ae4967721. The latest 2/1 result rejected the predicted trough. This new baseline constrains the beginning of a curve represented repeatedly in the candidate pool.

m12 at 2/1, 150 uL tests loading transfer after the 100-uL completion measured 16.83 rather than the previous 12.26-mL prediction. Its current prediction is 14.72, while the same-loading 20/1 anchor ca7513a424b1ad5dcd5a finishes at 21.88. The label tests whether the middle-loading interior response extends to higher loading.

m186 at 2/1, 100 uL starts a matched-ratio comparison with m190. Their measured 1/1 completions are both about 14.24, but at 20/1 they differ substantially in 5f1ae4e354b8b36ec691 and d1774335b45258bc173a. Current 2/1 predictions remain nearly identical. This locates where their recorded structure-condition responses diverge.

m56 at 100/1, 100 uL fills the loading interior between measured completions of 23.08 at 50 uL and 27.38 at 150 uL in 781b8d96d8bc7c124dc9 and 3016ab4b83227fcf83e4. Current predictions are nearly loading-invariant around 22.7. The label tests whether intermediate loading preserves the observed completion contrast while onset stays similar.

m56 at 50/1, 100 uL pairs with the selected 100/1 point to constrain a fixed-loading weak-eluent segment. The latest 150-uL 100/1 label exposed underestimated completion, whereas recent low-loading 10/1 and 20/1 labels were comparatively accurate. This asks where the additional completion growth develops.

m85 at 5/1, 100 uL tests a predicted completion of 12.70 against the measured low-loading 5/1 completion of 9.77 in 6da41d896190561e7545. With selected 10/1 and measured 20/1 at 100 uL, it identifies whether the model's completion excess starts early or only near the weak-eluent end.

m85 at 10/1, 100 uL completes the selected interior segment. Its prediction is 6.19/13.12, between the selected 5/1 condition and measured 20/1 response 8.60/16.51 in 35afc3cdfff849ffe8c9. This constrains onset and completion growth separately after the latest 50/1 completion was overpredicted by 4.73 mL.

m85 at 50/1, 150 uL tests whether the current 26.67-mL completion prediction represents a real high-loading increase. The 50- and 100-uL labels cd7c523e3df961c83524 and df93501912d2cfcfbc41 finish at 22.28 and 21.70. This is a direct loading-boundary test at the ratio where the latest prediction failed.

m84 at 20/1, 50 uL fills a frequently recurring missing benzoate condition before measured 30/1 completion 16.02 in ab49ee9538cdb7f47f70. The two recorded 10/1 labels c16aef24cbedd5b1b875 and 89b6013d19ba95312c59 differ, so this label helps constrain the segment without treating either earlier value as an exact curve.

m84 at 40/1, 50 uL tests the predicted completion increase to 22.05 from the measured 30/1 value of 16.02. The 100-uL 40/1 label 812adebe27af25dc2242 finishes at 22.47. Together with selected 20/1, it separates ratio curvature from loading transfer in a recurring input family.

m88 at pure EA, 100 uL establishes the missing baseline before measured 1/1 and 2/1 completions of 17.08 and 28.04 in c620129610cfe348f024 and ade065af3a515fc41105. Pairing it with m86 under each scaffold's recorded loading conditions tests whether their almost identical predicted baselines are informative transfer or excessive smoothing.

m88 at 1/1, 50 uL fills the amount contrast to the measured 100-uL 1/1 label c620129610cfe348f024 and precedes the 50-uL 2/1 label 27d20ccfd8f7234015f4. This constrains the strong-side transition in the meta-amino ester without inferring loading effects solely from its much later 5/1 response.

m86 at pure EA, 100 uL supplies the para-amino ester baseline corresponding to selected m88. Both currently predict completion near 9.58 mL, despite measured 5/1 completions of 57.53 and 61.83 in 3ccd6444c8a55917fbf8 and d2921349ba8d9cef15a4. Baseline labels test where their strong retention begins; recorded loading differences remain explicit.

m146 at pure EA, 100 uL explores ring-N onset transfer at the strong-solvent boundary. The prediction is 5.97/16.67, whereas the 50-uL baseline 8e999302c4d108ec9f19 measured 9.79/17.55. The 100-uL 2/1 and 5/1 anchors 2745c6978a8911fc3dda and 51f5ae6a991eea9e720e allow the new baseline to constrain the subsequent retention increase.

m146 at 5/1, 50 uL tests loading transfer in the ring-N regime against measured 100-uL response 31.31/60.95 in 51f5ae6a991eea9e720e. Its prediction is 30.79/60.43 with a broad onset quantile spread. This adds a targeted structural and loading reference in a historically difficult family, rather than applying a generic heteroatom correction.

m44 at pure EA, 150 uL starts a matched strong-side pair for ortho-methyl acetophenone. Its predicted completion is 11.48, below the measured same-loading pure-EA completions of 17.27 for m32 and 18.38 for m33 in 70dd45e8e1ff8116c181 and 003ad1a9637ac1b7c0fd. This tests the boundary of transferring those elevated baselines.

m44 at 1/1, 150 uL completes the matched pair. The predictor suggests only a shallow completion decrease from pure EA, unlike the larger measured decreases for m32 and m33 at this loading. Measuring both endpoints tests whether methyl substitution position changes the local response shape; steric shielding is a prior, not an established explanation.

m29 at 2/1, 100 uL starts a test of the predicted completion decrease from 12.85 here to 10.04 at selected 5/1. Measured 1/1 completion is 8.77 in a7a30ef771295dc6deed and 50/1 completion is 27.88 in f73fd2f4c55177304721. The missing pair determines whether an interior feature exists in this more crowded aromatic ketone.

m29 at 5/1, 100 uL completes the local pair. A measured decline would provide a useful boundary to the m32 low-loading increase; continued growth would reject another model-generated trough. The matched labels distinguish response curvature while holding molecular structure and all recorded loading conditions fixed.

m186 at 10/1, 100 uL extends the selected 2/1 condition toward measured 20/1 response 6.87/20.40 in 5f1ae4e354b8b36ec691. The model predicts 5.74/21.58 with broad onset quantiles and high CW distance. This tests whether onset remains early and completion approaches a plateau, or whether the missing interior differs from both neighboring predictions.

m190 at 2/1, 100 uL completes the selected matched-ratio comparison with m186. Their current completion predictions are nearly equal, although measured 20/1 completions are 29.88 and 20.40. The labels locate the divergence between these hydroxybromoaldehyde structure-condition combinations; density and loading-solvent volume prevent attribution to substitution position alone.

m0 at 1/1, 150 uL tests a predicted completion maximum near 15.96 mL before selected 2/1 and measured 5/1 completion 10.17 in 16cee53cbe16b60fb395. This extends exploration of unusual strong-side curvature to a heteroatom-free triaryl scaffold. The proposed maximum is prediction-only.

m0 at 2/1, 150 uL completes the fixed-loading segment, predicted at 6.57/14.11. With selected 1/1 and measured 5/1 and 50/1 rows 16cee53cbe16b60fb395 and 2c8bdc7f29ed47c7ce61, it tests whether onset and completion have distinct interior responses or the apparent maximum is a model artifact.

hypotheses.content: Identical recorded inputs can have substantially different labels in m81 and m32. m81's 5/1, 150-uL repeat finishes at 20.27 rather than 9.23 mL, weakening the proposed deterministic high-loading early-completion branch. m32's 100-uL 5/1 repeat attenuates, but does not by itself eliminate, its apparent central-loading completion maximum.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Further labels should constrain reproducible conditional means without repeatedly reinforcing an individual discrepant observation. The source of variation is unknown and cannot be assigned to an absent experimental variable.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m32's 5/1, 150-uL repeat reproduce its low completion, or move toward the higher completions seen at neighboring ratios and lower loadings?

hypotheses.content: Strong-side completion decreases and interior extrema among methyl-substituted aromatic ketones require scaffold- and loading-specific descriptions. Measured m32 and m33 decreases at 150 uL establish examples, but they do not establish the response of ortho-methyl m44 or the predicted 2/1-to-5/1 decrease in crowded m29.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched baseline and interior pairs can teach boundaries of graph-to-condition transfer. Carbonyl accessibility and aromatic substitution provide chemical priors, while the recorded responses determine whether a decrease or extremum actually occurs.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m32 retain an elevated pure-EA baseline at 50 uL, does m44 show a shallow or large decrease at 150 uL, and is m29's predicted interior decline measurable?

hypotheses.content: The m155 failure is concentrated around 1/1: both onset and completion were underestimated at 50 and 100 uL, with completion errors substantially larger. The accurate 50-uL 5/1 result argues against a uniform correction across its ratio curve or across nonpolar scaffolds.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The formerly inverted endpoint prediction exposed a real local prediction failure, but endpoint ordering alone could not identify its source. New baseline and amount-matched extension labels can localize the response and reduce inappropriate graph-wide offsets.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the 50-uL pure-EA baseline remain early, and does the 100-uL curve return to early completion by 5/1 despite its elevated 1/1 label?

hypotheses.content: Beta-carbonyl response shape depends on arrangement and loading. m82's measured 5/1 completions decrease from 36.83 to 29.34 to 25.28 mL across 50, 100 and 150 uL. Its 10/1 completions are later at all three amounts, while m26's newly measured 100-uL 10/1 completion is close to its 5/1 value rather than continuing a large decline. These patterns should not become a common beta-dicarbonyl template.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The latest large m82 completion miss suggests that loading transfer and transition location remain poorly constrained. New strong-side labels on m82, m95 and m78 test how far those relationships transfer across related carbonyl environments and recorded loading conditions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m82's loading dependence appear by 1/1, where does low-loading m95 begin its completion increase, and does m78 actually decrease from pure EA to 1/1?

hypotheses.content: Completion curvature and loading transfer differ across recurring benzoates. m56 shows later 100/1 completion at 150 than at 50 uL, whereas m85's measured 50/1 completions at 50 and 100 uL are close and below the latest 100-uL prediction. The missing m84 segment and m85 interior should be learned separately from these weak-eluent loading contrasts.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These input families recur extensively in the pool. Fixed-loading ratio segments and matched-ratio amount contrasts constrain different parts of the predictor, particularly where its loading predictions are nearly invariant despite measured differences.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does middle-loading m56 interpolate the 100/1 completion contrast, does high-loading m85 reproduce the lower-loading 50/1 regime, and where do the missing m84 and m85 completion increases occur?

hypotheses.content: Amino-ester structure-condition combinations have markedly different transitions: measured m86 and m88 5/1 completions at 100 uL are near 58–62 mL, whereas m89 and m104 have much earlier measured 5/1 completion. Their strong-solvent baselines need not differ similarly. m104 also has substantial variation among identical recorded 10/1 and 20/1 inputs, limiting deterministic loading interpretations.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The labels can separate baseline transfer from transition location and constrain loading interpolation. Amino position and possible local donor-acceptor interactions are priors; differing density, loading solvent and solvent volume prevent an isolated positional-effect claim.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are m86 and m88 pure-EA baselines as similar as predicted, does m88's low-loading 1/1 response track its middle-loading label, and where does m104's high-loading completion turn over?

hypotheses.content: The recorded m186 and m190 combinations have almost equal 1/1 completion at 100 uL but diverge at 20/1 and 50/1. The model still predicts almost equal 2/1 completion. The divergence may emerge after 2/1, or the missing early interior may already differ; this cannot be attributed solely to bromine position because loaded mass and loading-solvent volume differ.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The matched-ratio pair tests where graph and loading-condition transfer ceases to preserve completion similarity. The additional m186 10/1 label tests onset independently in a region with broad onset quantiles and high gradient-feature distance.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do their 2/1 labels remain similar, and does m186 retain early onset and approximately plateauing completion through 10/1?

feedback_interpretation: The latest repeats make reproducibility a stronger constraint on interpretation. m81's 5/1, 150-uL completion changed from 9.23 to 20.27 mL, joining the roughly 18.7-mL lower-loading labels and weakening the proposed deterministic high-loading branch. I therefore do not spend another batch tracing that branch. m32's repeated 100-uL 5/1 completion decreased from 18.56 to 15.05, attenuating the apparent central-loading maximum; its new 150-uL 10/1 completion of 21.36 and pure-EA completion of 17.27 still leave a consequential low 5/1 label whose reproducibility merits one targeted repeat. The m33 2/1 and 5/1 extensions were accurate, reducing the immediate value of more nearby extensions. m12's 2/1 completion of 16.83 rejected the predicted trough. m182 also lacked the predicted pronounced 2/1 trough, although its measured 1/1 value forms a shallower local minimum. These outcomes favor missing baselines and loading contrasts over repeatedly searching for extrema on already completed curves. m197's 150-uL pure-EA and 1/1 completions, 26.43 and 25.79, rejected its predicted strong-side maximum. m127's decreasing strong-side response transferred comparatively well to 100 uL. m104 instead exposed a substantial onset miss at 1/1, 100 uL, against a background of previously measured same-input variation, so its next missing high-loading point is treated as a boundary test rather than evidence for a general amino-ester correction. m82's 50-uL 5/1 completion of 36.83 was the largest latest completion miss and establishes a stronger loading contrast than predicted; related beta-carbonyl labels now emphasize transition location and transfer boundaries. m26's 10/1 completion was close to its 5/1 value, weakening continued-decline expectations. m64 and m65 now agree closely in measured interior completion and largely in onset, weakening the proposed persistent onset distinction and lowering further haloketone-interior priority. The m155 measurements identify a genuine, mainly completion-side failure around 1/1, while its accurate 5/1 extension localizes the concern. Finally, the m56 weak-edge completion underestimate and m85 weak-edge overestimate support separate ester loading tests rather than a shared correction.
batch_rationale: The 32 choices form specific local experiments around gaps that remain useful after the latest feedback. One m32 repeat tests whether a response feature worth learning is reproducible; other identical-input candidates are generally left aside because repeated measurements have already demonstrated substantial variation in several families. Matched strong-side pairs on m44, m29, m78 and m0 distinguish predicted decreases or maxima from smoother responses, with measured anchors defining what each answer would teach. The m155 pair directly localizes a demonstrated joint-endpoint failure. The m82 and m95 additions test how loading and carbonyl arrangement affect the start of completion growth, while the amino-ester and hydroxyaldehyde comparisons test boundaries of structural transfer under explicitly different recorded loading conditions. The m56, m85 and m84 segments address common Row inputs through both ratio-response and amount-response labels. The m12 additions constrain a frequent early-onset family after a predicted trough failed, and the m146 labels add ring-N baseline and loading coverage in a historically difficult retention regime. This allocation reduces follow-up where recent labels were accurate and increases effort where a new label can distinguish competing conditional explanations. The expected benefit is improved retrained V1/V2 prediction across recurring rows and related structures, with onset and completion assessed separately. Quantile spreads and CW distance are supporting diagnostics, not calibrated epistemic uncertainty; elution interval width is not treated as uncertainty. No unrecorded concentration, pH, flow or column variables are assumed.
